chapter: The 1920s road: dance style and management
title: Buck's passive role and Bubbles as a father to him
summary: Bubbles handled all the business; Buck was satisfied as he was and would have stayed in Kentucky.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: Did Buck have any -- well, you were doing most of the handling of the goods --
What was Buck doing this whole time?
Nothin', what's he going to do.
Did he have any idea what was happening? Did he care, did he get --

No, he didn't have that kind of mind. He was satisfied as he was. Just like Chuck would be satisfied as he is if nobody enlightened him on anything, he'd be stay put. And that's the same way Buck was. I had to get him out of Kentucky. I had to teach him how to be and act in public. I was just like a father to him. So anyway, he --
What do you mean you had to get him out of Kentucky?
He would still be in Kentucky if it weren't for me. Why would he go? Why would he go?
What first attracted you to him?

His piana playing, his piana playing, that attracted me. Then I wanted to sing while he played piano. And that developed the act, it developed a whole lot of things. No use to leave him behind if I have to bring my own music with me, no use leaving him behind. I wanted to take him to the
carnival. I wanted to take him with the carnival, but he was too young.
